:::writing{variant="document" id="48317" title="BUILD 01H — Cognitive Runtime Integration & Unified Cognition"}
BUILD 01H — Cognitive Runtime Integration & Unified Cognition
Mission
Build the Cognitive Runtime Integration layer that unifies the completed offline cognitive subsystems into one coherent, deterministic cognitive cycle.
This build is NOT a new brain, NOT an LLM integration, NOT an APK/native build, and NOT a redesign.
The purpose is:

Make the already-built cognitive organs operate together through explicit contracts so Jarvis can move through a complete internal cognition cycle without bypassing or duplicating any subsystem.

Current completed foundations include:

Build 01A — Cognitive State + Working Memory
Build 01B — Goal + Planning
Build 01C — Execution
Build 01D — Immune & Resilience
Build 01E — Capability Fabric
Build 01F — Capability-Resolved Planning & Execution
Build 01G — Cognitive Continuity & Memory Lifecycle

Build 01H must integrate these existing mechanisms.

1. ABSOLUTE RULES
Rule 1 — Do not redesign previous builds
Treat 01A–01G as established architecture and contracts.
Do not replace existing:

CognitiveState
WorkingMemory
AttentionEngine
IntentInference
CognitiveContextBuilder
GoalPlanner
DecisionEngine
PlanGraph
ExecutionEngine / capability-aware executor
ImmuneSystem
CapabilityFabric
MemoryConsolidator
MemoryUpdateEngine
MemoryConflictResolver
ContinuityManager
ContinuityPort
CognitiveEvent bus
FailureSurface
StoragePort
existing model/provider abstractions

Extend existing contracts only when absolutely necessary.
Prefer adapters, orchestration, and additive interfaces.
Rule 2 — One new subsystem only
Create one subsystem:
com.jarvis.app.cognitive.runtime
Its job is orchestration.
Do not create duplicate planners, memories, event buses, execution systems, capability registries, failure systems, or context systems.
Rule 3 — No real model yet
Do NOT implement:

Qwen3 integration
llama.cpp runtime
GGUF loading
model inference
cloud models
LLM reasoning
prompt-generation logic

The runtime must work entirely with deterministic test doubles.
Rule 4 — No APK/native/runtime work
Do NOT:

build APKs
modify MainActivity
wire Android UI
introduce native dependencies
introduce JNI
move voice into the runtime
add camera/screen vision
add cloud services

This remains a pure JVM cognitive build.
Rule 5 — No autonomous infinite loop
There must be no:
while(true)

agent loop.
Every cognitive cycle must have explicit boundaries and termination conditions.

2. CORE PROBLEM
Today Jarvis has many cognitive organs, but they can still be invoked independently.
01H creates the missing orchestration contract:
Input
  ↓
Perceive / normalize
  ↓
Intent
  ↓
Context
  ↓

  ↓

  ↓

  ↓

  ↓

The runtime should coordinate these stages without replacing them.

3. NEW CORE CONTRACT
Create:
CognitiveRuntime
The main orchestration boundary.
It should expose a bounded operation similar to:
suspend fun runCycle(input: CognitiveInput): CognitiveCycleResult

Do not force this exact API if the repository's conventions require a better shape, but preserve the same concept.

4. COGNITIVE INPUT
Create a structured input type.
Example dimensions:
user input
source
timestamp
session identity
environment information
optional current task
optional external observations
optional interruption/cancellation state

Do not reduce the input to a String-only API.
The runtime must be able to receive structured observations later.

5. COGNITIVE CYCLE
Create an explicit state machine for the cognitive cycle.
Suggested states:
IDLE
INGESTING
INTERPRETING
RECONSTRUCTING
ATTENDING
GOAL_FORMING
DECIDING
PLANNING
EXECUTING
OBSERVING_RESULT
CONSOLIDATING
COMPLETED
BLOCKED
FAILED
CANCELLED

Use a deterministic transition table.
Invalid transitions must be rejected.
The cycle must never silently jump between stages.

6. PIPELINE ORCHESTRATION
The runtime must coordinate existing mechanisms in this order.
Phase A — Ingest
Accept CognitiveInput.
Validate structural requirements.
Create the initial cycle state.
Emit a runtime-start event.

Phase B — Intent
Use the existing:
IntentInference
Do not implement a second intent engine.
Capture:

inferred intent
confidence
ambiguity
entities
interpretation metadata

Low-confidence results must remain explicit.
Do not manufacture certainty.

Phase C — Continuity Reconstruction
Use the existing:
ContinuityPort
Request bounded reconstruction relevant to the current input.
The runtime must never dump the complete memory store into cognition.
Carry forward:

current truths
relevant history
conflicts
unknowns
temporal context
confidence


Phase D — Working Memory
Use existing:
WorkingMemory
Insert/activate only information relevant to the current cognitive cycle.
Do not copy the entire continuity reconstruction into working memory.
Respect existing:

capacity
activation
relevance
priority
decay
eviction


Phase E — Context
Use:
AttentionEngine+CognitiveContextBuilder
Construct the bounded reasoning context.
The runtime should provide the builder with:

current input
intent
active goal
working-memory state
attention results
continuity reconstruction
relevant observations
resource state
capability state

Do not create another context representation.

7. GOAL / DECISION / PLAN
Use the existing:
GoalPlannerDecisionEnginePlanGraph
The runtime determines whether the input requires:
response only
decision
goal
plan
execution

Do not force every input through a full plan.
For example:

→ cognitive response path

"What is X?"
→ interpretation + context path

"Remind me to do X"
→ goal/task path

"Find X and summarize it"
→ plan + execution path

This classification must be deterministic for tests.

8. CAPABILITY-AWARE EXECUTION
When execution is required, the runtime must use the existing:
PlanGraph→ capability-aware executor→ CapabilityFabric
It must not directly call a capability implementation.
The chain must remain:
Goal
→ PlanGraph
→ execution
→ ActionRequest
→ capability resolution
→ CapabilityInvoker
→ result

Respect:

capability lifecycle
permissions
availability
dependencies
circuit breakers
degradation
failure surface
partial failure
replanning


9. IMMUNE INTEGRATION
The runtime must not implement its own failure system.
All execution failures must flow through the established immune architecture.
The runtime should react to:

unavailable capability
dependency failure
timeout
cancellation
partial failure
degraded state
execution failure
persistence failure

The runtime must distinguish:
FAILED
BLOCKED
CANCELLED
DEGRADED
PARTIALLY_COMPLETED
COMPLETED

Do not collapse these into one boolean.

10. OUTCOME OBSERVATION
After execution, collect the structured outcome.
Capture:

actions attempted
actions completed
failures
partial results
replan activity
capability used
duration
confidence
evidence
final plan state

Feed the result back into the existing decision/outcome mechanisms.
Do not invent a second outcome model unless the existing structures truly cannot represent the cycle-level result.

11. MEMORY CONTINUITY UPDATE
At the end of the cycle:
Use the existing memory lifecycle.
Where appropriate:
experience
→ ExperienceRecord
→ MemoryConsolidator
→ promotion / reject / defer
→ update / supersede / conflict
→ persistence

Do NOT automatically store every interaction.
Memory admission must remain governed by the existing promotion lifecycle.
The runtime is an orchestrator, not a memory engine.

12. COGNITIVE STATE UPDATE
At cycle completion, synchronize CognitiveState.
The final state should accurately reflect:

current intent
current goal
active subgoals
plan
decision
working-memory references
attention
uncertainty
resource state
capability state
relevant continuity information
last outcome

Do not introduce a parallel runtime state that becomes the real source of truth.
CognitiveState remains the cognitive state source.
The runtime may have a temporary CognitiveCycleState for orchestration, but it must not duplicate long-lived cognitive state.

13. EVENT SYSTEM
Use the existing:
CognitiveEvent
Do NOT create another event bus.
Add only the minimum runtime event types required.
Suggested events:
CognitiveCycleStarted
CognitivePhaseChanged
CognitiveCycleBlocked
CognitiveCycleCompleted
CognitiveCycleFailed
CognitiveCycleCancelled

Every important transition must be observable.
Events must contain structured data, not only log strings.

14. CANCELLATION
Cancellation must be a first-class behavior.
External cancellation must:

stop the current cycle
cancel downstream work when possible
NOT be converted into an ordinary failure
preserve completed work
leave the system in a valid state
emit CognitiveCycleCancelled

Follow the cancellation behavior already established by the execution/capability layers.

15. FAILURE CONTAINMENT
A failure in one phase must not corrupt unrelated cognitive state.
Examples:
continuity failure
→ cognition may continue with bounded missing context

capability failure
→ execution fails/replans
→ cognitive runtime remains healthy

memory persistence failure
→ cycle result remains usable
→ persistence failure is observable

optional subsystem unavailable
→ degrade gracefully

cycle cancellation
→ cancellation, not failure

Use existing immune semantics wherever applicable.

16. DETERMINISM
Given the same:
input
initial CognitiveState
working-memory contents
continuity state
capability state
resource state
configuration

the runtime should produce the same structural result.
Do not include nondeterministic data in comparison-sensitive results.
Timestamps may exist for observability but must not alter deterministic decision paths.

17. CYCLE RESULT
Create a structured:
CognitiveCycleResult
It should describe at minimum:
cycleId
status
interpretedIntent
goal
plan
decision
executionSummary
continuitySummary
memoryChanges
failure/blocked information
final cognitive state
events/observations needed for diagnostics

Avoid duplicating existing objects.
Prefer references or existing structures.

Minimum coverage:

empty input

low-confidence intent

partial success

Persistence

corrupted persistence degrades safely

Determinism

same initial state + same input → same structural cycle result

Event ordering
Verify the event stream follows the cognitive phases deterministically.

Build Jarvis's system-wide Diagnostic Fabric before adding another major cognitive subsystem.

This is NOT a testing framework.

- Jarvis can know what is happening internally.
- Jarvis can know what failed and where.

1. Graphify is the big one
This is the one most directly aimed at the problem you're describing.
Graphify builds a persistent knowledge graph of the repository instead of making the coding agent repeatedly rediscover the architecture through grep/file reading. Its current documentation specifically describes code, classes, functions, imports, references and typed relationships, with the graph persisting across sessions. 
That maps extremely well to Jarvis because your repository is already large and highly interconnected.
The important effect isn't necessarily that Claude generates code faster per token. It's that Claude can spend fewer tokens reconstructing context, which means more of its context budget goes toward the actual implementation.
Graphify also supports multimodal inputs such as PDFs, Markdown, screenshots, diagrams and images, which is unusually relevant to your project because your Jarvis architecture isn't only source code. 
For your project: very high value.
2. Karpathy Skills should improve Claude's execution discipline
The skill isn't an acceleration engine in the hardware sense.
It changes how Claude approaches coding tasks: explicit plans, strong success criteria, verification loops, and avoiding assumptions. 
That matters for Jarvis because your biggest waste isn't necessarily typing speed. It's:

Claude explores → misunderstands something → edits wrong area → discovers problem → backtracks → rereads files → burns context.

The skill is designed to reduce that kind of wandering.
So I'd use it, but merge its principles into your existing Jarvis CLAUDE.md rather than blindly replacing your instructions. The plugin is explicitly installable into Claude Code or its guidance can be appended to a project CLAUDE.md. 
3. Freebuff is different
Freebuff is not an optimization layer for Claude Code. It's an alternative coding agent with its own agent loop, model pool and specialized subagents. Its current materials describe nine specialized workers, including a file-picker, reviewer and browser-use agent. 
That makes it interesting for parallelization.
For example:
Claude Code
    ↓
main Jarvis implementation

Freebuff
    ↓
repository exploration
dependency investigation
alternative implementation research
code review
documentation generation

That can increase your overall throughput, but it doesn't magically make the same Claude Code session faster.
And there is a potentially important advantage: Freebuff advertises a file-picker subagent that builds a local code map and returns ranked relevant files. That's conceptually similar to the exact context-selection problem Graphify is attacking. 
So I wouldn't replace Claude Code with Freebuff.
I'd use it as a secondary worker when the task can be parallelized.
4. OpenAlternative is the least direct
OpenAlternative is primarily a directory/discovery system. Its current Claude Code alternatives page lists things like OpenCode, Pi, OpenHands, Zed and Cline. 
That's useful because we can use it to continuously ask:

"Is there now a tool that solves one of our bottlenecks better?"

But installing random alternatives into your Jarvis workflow would probably make things slower, because you'd accumulate overlapping tools and additional context/configuration.
So treat OpenAlternative as a research catalog, not as another permanent component.

What I'd actually do for Jarvis
I'd build a Claude Code acceleration stack, not just install four websites.
                         JARVIS REPO
                              │
                    ┌─────────┴─────────┐
                    │      Graphify      │
                    │ persistent code   │
                    │   knowledge graph  │
                    └─────────┬─────────┘
                              ↓
                       Claude Code
                              │
                    Karpathy discipline
                              │
                 ┌────────────┴────────────┐
                 ↓                         ↓
        main implementation          targeted tasks
                 │                         │
                 │                  Freebuff / other
                 │                    secondary agents
                 ↓
             Git / repo
                 │
                 ↓
           Jarvis milestone

The important combination is Graphify + better agent instructions + selective parallel agents.
And there's an even bigger opportunity for you
Because we're deliberately postponing your final Diagnostic Fabric until Stage 16, we can use these tools as the development-time equivalent of that system.
Graphify gives Claude a persistent structural map.
Karpathy Skills makes Claude operate more deliberately.
A secondary agent can investigate/review in parallel.
Then Claude Code stays the primary builder.
That means we aren't changing Jarvis's architecture prematurely, but we are improving the machinery used to build Jarvis.
My recommendation
Install Graphify first.
Then integrate the Karpathy principles into your existing Claude Code project instructions.
Then use Freebuff only for tasks that can genuinely run in parallel.
Keep OpenAlternative as the place we mine for future upgrades.
I would not replace Claude Code.
The current evidence strongly suggests Graphify is the one that directly attacks your biggest problem: repeated codebase re-exploration and context waste. 
And because Jarvis has become large and interconnected, that is much more valuable than simply switching to another coding agent.

The builder must be able to request research rather than pretending it already knows everything.


MECHANISM EXTRACTION

This is critical.
Research must not end with:

Instead:
Discovery→ mechanism→ abstraction→ strengths→ weaknesses→ reusable principle→ Jarvis-native design
This is how Jarvis eventually discovers algorithms instead of merely importing software.

→ same environment→ same workload→ same measurement→ compare

45. JARVIS SELF-EVOLUTION BOUNDARY

When the target is Jarvis itself:

LIVE JARVIS
    ↓
SNAPSHOT
    ↓
MUTATED JARVIS ENVIRONMENT
    ↓
CHANGE
    ↓
BUILD
    ↓
RUN
    ↓
BENCHMARK
    ↓
COMPARE TO CURRENT
    ↓
PROMOTION DECISION

Never:

Jarvis rewrites live Jarvis directly.

That boundary is permanent.

---

46. CAPABILITY FABRIC INTEGRATION

All development operations should eventually be capabilities.

Examples:

- READ_FILE
- WRITE_FILE
- PATCH_FILE
- SEARCH_CODE
- QUERY_GRAPH
- RUN_COMMAND
- BUILD_PROJECT
- START_PROCESS
- STOP_PROCESS
- CREATE_ENVIRONMENT
- DESTROY_ENVIRONMENT
- RUN_BENCHMARK
- DEPLOY
- ROLLBACK
- INSPECT_FAILURE

Use the existing Capability Fabric.

Do not create a new tool registry.

---

47. EXECUTION INTEGRATION

Development operations must flow through the existing execution architecture where applicable:

PlanGraph
→ ActionRequest
→ Capability
→ CapabilityInvoker
→ result

Do not bypass:

- immune layer
- permissions
- capability lifecycle
- resource policy
- failure surface

The Building System is an extension of Jarvis's existing execution organism, not a parallel execution architecture.

---

48. PERMISSIONS

Development operations must have explicit permission categories.

Examples:

- READ_WORKSPACE
- WRITE_WORKSPACE
- EXECUTE_PROCESS
- INSTALL_DEPENDENCY
- CREATE_ENVIRONMENT
- DEPLOY
- PROMOTE
- ROLLBACK

The permission system should distinguish:

EXPERIMENTAL PERMISSION

from:

LIVE-SYSTEM PERMISSION

Experimental permissions may be broader.

Live promotion permissions must be stricter.

---

49. LIVE SYSTEM PROTECTION

The builder must know the difference between:

EXPERIMENTAL
STAGED
LIVE

Rules:

EXPERIMENTAL

Anything is permitted within configured environment limits.

STAGED

Deployment candidate; still isolated.

LIVE

Controlled and protected.

No experimental mutation should silently cross that boundary.

---

50. DEPLOYMENT ESCALATION

A deployment should explicitly progress:

EXPERIMENT
→ CANDIDATE
→ STAGED
→ LIVE

Promotion is a deliberate transition.

Rollback can move:

LIVE
→ PREVIOUS LIVE

without deleting evidence.

51. BUILDER API

Expose a high-level operation similar to:

buildProject(request)

The request may specify:

- target
- objective
- constraints
- environment policy
- resource budget
- deadline
- deployment policy
- success criteria

Return:

BuildResult

with:

- success
- candidate
- environment
- artifacts
- benchmark
- failures
- changes
- promotion recommendation
- evidence
- lessons

Adapt names to repository conventions.

Do not force these exact class names if equivalent domain abstractions already exist.

52. EXPERIMENT API

Provide:

It should:

create environment
→ apply candidate
→ execute
→ observe
→ benchmark
→ preserve evidence
→ destroy or retain

The experiment must have a lifecycle and persistent identity.

---

53. DEPLOY API

Provide:

deploy(candidate)

with explicit policy gates.

Never allow deployment to bypass promotion policy.

Deployment must remain separate from promotion.

---

54. ROLLBACK API

Provide:

and preserve:

- reason
- source deployment
- target version
- evidence
- resulting state

Rollback must itself produce an auditable operation record.

55. ENVIRONMENT DESTRUCTION

When an environment is destroyed:

Delete runtime state.

Preserve:

- experiment metadata
- source snapshot
- benchmark results
- failure evidence
- lessons
- candidate lineage
- relevant artifacts

The reality disappears.

Its knowledge does not.

56. REPRODUCIBILITY

Every experiment must be reproducible as far as practical.

Record:

- source version
- environment specification
- dependency versions
- configuration
- model used
- worker configuration
- algorithm candidate
- benchmark workload
- resource policy

Jarvis must be able to recreate an experiment from its recorded specification rather than relying on hidden state.

62. CANDIDATE LINEAGE

Candidates must form a genealogy.

Example:

CURRENT
 ├── Candidate-A
 │    ├── Candidate-A1

 └── Candidate-B
      └── Candidate-B1

Jarvis must be able to determine:

- parent
- descendants
- modifications
- benchmark differences
- why a branch was selected or rejected

This is essential for future algorithm discovery and self-evolution.

63. EXPERIMENT SPECIFICATION

64. OPERATION JOURNAL

- rollback
- destruction

Store structured metadata plus references to retained evidence.

65. EVIDENCE MODEL

Create a common Evidence abstraction.

- deployment health
- model output
- research finding
- comparison result

Every important development decision should be traceable to evidence.

This becomes critical when Jarvis later evaluates whether a change is actually an improvement.

66. OBSERVATION MODEL

Create structured observations rather than passing raw logs directly into cognition.

An observation may contain:

- timestamp
- source
- environment

The Observation layer should be usable by:

- diagnosis
- benchmarking

67. HEALTH MODEL

The Building System should expose health information for:

- environment
- workspace
- build

- deployment

Do not create the final system-wide Stage 16 Diagnostic Fabric here.

This build only needs the local health information required to operate the Building System.

68. RESOURCE GOVERNANCE

Integrate with the existing ResourceGovernor.

Every major operation should be resource-aware:

- model invocation
- worker creation
- environment creation
- build
- process execution
- benchmark
- deployment

Before expensive work:

resource availability
→ estimate cost
→ authorize
→ execute
→ record actual cost

This allows Jarvis to choose cheaper mechanisms when they are sufficient.

69. COMPUTE ADAPTATION

The system should eventually support adaptive execution:

LOW COMPLEXITY
→ deterministic mechanism

MODERATE
→ retrieval / small model

HIGH
→ reasoning model

NOVEL / UNCERTAIN
→ research + deep reasoning

PARALLELIZABLE
→ bounded workers

This is where the LFM research principles become useful.

Do not hardcode one model.

70. WORKER ORCHESTRATION

Workers must be controlled by the central Development Orchestrator.

The orchestrator owns:

- worker creation
- task assignment
- context allocation
- resource allocation
- cancellation
- result collection
- conflict handling
- worker termination

Workers do not create uncontrolled workers indefinitely.

---

71. WORKER CONTRACT

Every worker must receive a bounded task contract:

- taskId
- objective
- inputs
- allowed capabilities
- workspace/environment
- resource budget
- deadline
- expected output

Every worker returns:

- status
- result
- evidence
- changes
- blockers
- confidence
- recommended next action

This keeps orchestration deterministic and inspectable.

---

72. CONFLICT RESOLUTION

If workers produce conflicting results:

Do not blindly merge them.

The orchestrator should:

1. identify conflict
2. preserve both results
3. compare evidence
4. request additional analysis if necessary
5. select or synthesize a result
6. record the decision

Worker disagreement becomes evidence, not chaos.

---

73. RESEARCH WORKER

The research worker should produce structured research output:

- question
- sources
- findings
- mechanisms
- limitations
- alternatives
- confidence
- recommendation

The worker should not directly modify Jarvis.

Its result returns to the orchestrator.

---

74. REPOSITORY WORKER

The repository worker should answer questions such as:

- where is X implemented?
- what depends on X?
- what files are relevant?
- what architecture is involved?
- what could this change affect?

It should prioritize Graphify/repository intelligence rather than repeatedly scanning everything.

---

75. IMPLEMENTATION WORKER

The implementation worker may modify only its assigned environment/workspace.

It returns:

- changes
- files affected
- build status
- blockers
- evidence

It cannot promote its own work.

---

76. REVIEW WORKER

The review worker evaluates:

- requested behavior
- architecture
- compatibility
- unintended changes
- resource impact
- candidate quality

Its output becomes evidence for candidate evaluation.

---

77. BENCHMARK WORKER

The benchmark worker runs the defined workload against candidates using identical measurement rules.

It must not modify candidate implementation merely to improve its score.

---

78. DEPLOYMENT WORKER

The deployment worker handles deployment mechanics.

It does not decide whether a candidate deserves promotion.

Promotion remains a separate policy decision.

---

79. WORKER CANCELLATION

Any worker must be cancellable.

Cancellation must:

- stop execution
- release resources
- preserve useful evidence
- update task state
- avoid leaving orphan processes

---

80. DEADLINE / BUDGET CONTROL

Every development session should have:

- time budget
- compute budget
- memory budget
- worker budget
- mutation budget
- repair iteration budget

The system must degrade gracefully when the budget is exhausted.

It should report:

"Insufficient budget to complete."

rather than entering an endless loop.

81. DEVELOPMENT STATE MACHINE

Create an explicit DevelopmentSession lifecycle:

82. RECOVERY

If the process itself is interrupted:

Jarvis should be able to recover the DevelopmentSession from persistent state.

It should determine:

- last known state
- active environment
- unfinished operation
- surviving processes
- retained evidence
- next safe action

Never assume that an interrupted process completed successfully.

83. IDEMPOTENCY

Operations that may be retried should be idempotent where practical.

Examples:

- environment initialization
- dependency installation
- artifact registration
- state transitions
- deployment preparation

Repeated execution must not corrupt the development state.

84. CONCURRENCY CONTROL

Prevent multiple workers from silently modifying the same workspace state.

- locks
- change sets
- branch/candidate isolation
- merge/reconciliation

Prefer separate candidate environments for competing implementations.

A ChangeSet contains:

87. ALGORITHM LAB

88. BASELINE SYSTEM

Every benchmarkable candidate needs a baseline where appropriate.

Compare:

BASELINE
vs
CANDIDATE

using the same workload and resource conditions.

The baseline must be preserved so future improvements do not accidentally become regressions.

---

89. REGRESSION PROTECTION

A candidate must be evaluated not only for the feature being changed but also for important known behavior.

Record:

- baseline behavior
- candidate behavior
- regression signals

A faster implementation that silently destroys important behavior is not automatically an improvement.

---

90. PROMOTION DECISION MODEL

Promotion should combine evidence rather than rely on one score.

Consider:

- correctness
- required behavior
- benchmark improvement
- resource cost
- reliability
- compatibility
- regression risk
- confidence
- reversibility

The result should be:

PROMOTE
REJECT
NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE

Do not force a binary decision when evidence is insufficient.

91. PROMOTION RECORD

Every promotion must create a persistent record containing:

- candidate
- previous live version
- new live version
- evidence
- decision
- reason
- timestamp
- promotion policy
- rollback target

This is part of Jarvis's future self-understanding.

92. DEPLOYMENT OBSERVATION

After deployment:

→ observe
→ compare against expected behavior

→ diagnose
→ decide
→ rollback or repair

93. POST-DEPLOYMENT LEARNING

After a deployment reaches a stable outcome:

experience
→ evaluate
→ extract lesson

The system should learn from both:

and:

failed deployments / rollbacks.

94. SELF-DEVELOPMENT LOOP

Once the generic system is working, Jarvis can target itself:

        ↓

        ↓

The important point is:

Jarvis does not need to modify himself directly.

He creates alternatives and evaluates them.

95. SELF-EVOLUTION SAFETY

Self-evolution must remain bounded.

Required controls:

- environment isolation
- resource limits
- change limits
- iteration limits
- promotion gates
- rollback

- evidence

Do not implement an uncontrolled recursive self-modification loop.

98. OFFLINE-FIRST

The Building System must remain useful offline.

It should be capable of:

- repository analysis
- code modification
- local builds
- local execution
- local experiments
- local benchmarks
- local deployment
- local memory
- local model use

without requiring cloud services.

Cloud Code is not a dependency of Jarvis.

99. CLOUD CODE BOUNDARY

Cloud Code is an external development accelerator.

It may be used NOW to build Jarvis.

It must NOT become a runtime dependency of Jarvis.

The finished Jarvis Building System must be capable of performing its own development lifecycle using Jarvis-native capabilities.

Cloud Code may later become:

- an external research source
- an external worker
- an optional development capability

but never the foundation of Jarvis's existence.

107. SECURITY / TRUST BOUNDARY

Treat the environment boundary as a trust boundary.

The system must know:

LIVE
STAGED
EXPERIMENTAL

and enforce that distinction through capability/policy checks.

Do not rely solely on the model "remembering" not to modify live state.

Architecture must enforce it.

---

108. SECRETS

Never copy live credentials into experimental environments unnecessarily.

Secrets should be provided through controlled mechanisms.

Do not persist secrets inside:

- experiment logs
- evidence
- memory
- source snapshots
- candidate metadata

---

109. ARTIFACT PROMOTION

An artifact should not become a live artifact merely because it exists.

Artifact lifecycle:

CREATED
→ VERIFIED
→ CANDIDATE
→ STAGED
→ PROMOTED
→ RETIRED

Retired artifacts should remain traceable for rollback where necessary.

---

110. CLEANUP

The Building System must clean up:

- orphan environments
- orphan processes
- abandoned workers
- temporary files
- expired artifacts
- stale sessions

Cleanup must preserve evidence required for learning and lineage.

---

111. RECOVERY AFTER CRASH

If Jarvis crashes while an experiment is active:

On restart:

1. discover persisted sessions
2. identify incomplete operations
3. inspect environment state
4. detect orphan processes
5. reconcile state
6. mark uncertain operations appropriately
7. continue or safely terminate

Never assume success after an interrupted operation.

---

112. FAILURE CATEGORIES

Integrate with the existing FailureSurface rather than creating a competing failure architecture.

failure pattern
→ diagnosis
→ repair
→ result
→ reusable lesson

research question

→ result

decision

→ evidence
→ consequences

116. DEVELOPMENT CONTINUITY

If a development session is interrupted, Jarvis should be able to resume from:

objective
+ current state
+ plan
+ environment
+ evidence
+ pending operation
+ previous lessons

rather than restarting from zero.

117. TOKEN ECONOMICS

The Building System must minimize expensive model context.

Use:

- Graphify retrieval
- symbol-level retrieval
- file-level retrieval
- semantic retrieval
- memory retrieval
- task summaries
- evidence compression
- worker-specific context
- persistent external state

Never use model context as the database.

118. CONTEXT COMPRESSION

RAW EVENTS
→ summarize
→ important decisions
→ unresolved issues
→ current state
→ evidence references

Keep raw evidence separately when required.

119. MODEL ROUTING

Model selection should be a capability of the cognitive/resource layer.

The Building System requests:

"reasoning capability"

rather than:

"call model X."

The ModelManager decides what model/provider is appropriate.

This preserves provider independence.

Future local models must be able to replace the external route.

121. GRAPHIFY COMPATIBILITY

144. FINAL DESIGN PRINCIPLE

The Mutated Environment is not where Jarvis "tests code."

It is where Jarvis is allowed to create alternative realities.

Within those realities he can:

- change architecture
- change algorithms
- change models
- change dependencies
- change tools
- change memory strategies
- change capabilities
- change orchestration
- break everything
- fix everything
- benchmark everything
- compare everything

Then only the strongest candidate is promoted.

That is how Jarvis can eventually evolve without repeatedly risking the organism that is already alive.

---

145. WHAT THIS BUILD IS NOT

Do NOT turn this into:

- another chatbot
- another coding assistant
- another IDE
- another generic agent framework
- another multi-agent swarm
- another sandbox library
- another CI/CD system
- another memory system
- another research tool
- another model router

These mechanisms may exist internally where useful.

The result must be a single Jarvis-native development organism.

---

146. WHAT THIS BUILD ENABLES

After this build, future Jarvis development should no longer fundamentally depend on manually implementing every new capability.

Instead:

Need capability
→ research
→ mechanism
→ design
→ build
→ experiment
→ benchmark
→ candidate
→ promotion

Need better capability
→ create alternative
→ benchmark against current
→ promote only if better

Need new application
→ define outcome
→ construct environment
→ build application
→ deploy

Need to improve Jarvis
→ fork Jarvis
→ mutate candidate
→ build
→ observe
→ compare
→ promote

This is the transition from:

"AI that can use tools"

to:

"AI that possesses a system for constructing and evolving tools, software, capabilities, and eventually itself."

Build this as one coherent system.



You:

JARVIS SELF-EVOLUTION BOUNDARY

When the target is Jarvis itself:  
LIVE JARVIS    ↓SNAPSHOT    ↓MUTATED JARVIS ENVIRONMENT    ↓CHANGE    ↓BUILD    ↓RUN    ↓BENCHMARK    ↓COMPARE TO CURRENT    ↓PROMOTION DECISION

immune layer

capability lifecycle

failure surface

The Building System is an extension of Jarvis's existing execution organism, not a parallel execution architecture.

EXPERIMENTAL PERMISSION  
from:  
LIVE-SYSTEM PERMISSION  
Experimental permissions may be broader.  
Live promotion permissions must be stricter.  


LIVE SYSTEM PROTECTION

The builder must know the difference between:  
EXPERIMENTALSTAGEDLIVE  
Rules:  
EXPERIMENTAL  
Anything is permitted within configured environment limits.  
STAGED  
Deployment candidate; still isolated.  
LIVE  
Controlled and protected.  
No experimental mutation should silently cross that boundary.  


DEPLOYMENT ESCALATION

A deployment should explicitly progress:  
EXPERIMENT→ CANDIDATE→ STAGED→ LIVE  
Promotion is a deliberate transition.  
Rollback can move:  
LIVE→ PREVIOUS LIVE  
without deleting evidence.

benchmark results  
resource usage  
evidence  
status  
promotion eligibility

Possible states:  
PROPOSED→ BUILDING→ RUNNING→ EVALUATED→ PROMOTABLE→ PROMOTED  
or:  
REJECTEDFAILEDABANDONED  


CANDIDATE LINEAGE

Candidates must form a genealogy.  
Example:  
CURRENT ├── Candidate-A │    ├── Candidate-A1 │    └── Candidate-A2 │ └── Candidate-B      └── Candidate-B1  
Jarvis must be able to determine:  

parent  
descendants  
modifications  
benchmark differences  
why a branch was selected or rejected

This is essential for future algorithm discovery and self-evolution.  


EXPERIMENT SPECIFICATION

Create a declarative ExperimentSpecification.  
It should define:  

objective  
target  
base state  
candidate changes  
environment requirements  
resource limits  
workload  
success criteria  
benchmark criteria  
timeout  
iteration limits  
retention policy

The specification should be serializable.  
An experiment should be describable without depending on the active model context.  


OPERATION JOURNAL

Create a persistent operation journal for the Building System.  
Record major operations such as:  

environment creation  
environment mutation  
file modification  
command execution  
build  
repair  
benchmark  
deployment  
promotion  
rollback  
destruction

Do not store enormous raw logs indefinitely.  
Store structured metadata plus references to retained evidence.  


EVIDENCE MODEL

Create a common Evidence abstraction.  
Evidence may represent:  

command output  
compiler error  
runtime observation  
benchmark result  
resource measurement  
deployment health  
model output  
research finding  
comparison result

Every important development decision should be traceable to evidence.  
This becomes critical when Jarvis later evaluates whether a change is actually an improvement.  


OBSERVATION MODEL

Create structured observations rather than passing raw logs directly into cognition.  
An observation may contain:  

timestamp  
source  
environment  
process  
metric  
value  
severity  
context  
evidence reference

The Observation layer should be usable by:  

diagnosis  
benchmarking  
memory  
self-diagnostics  
future improvement



HEALTH MODEL

The Building System should expose health information for:  

environment  
workspace  
build  
process  
artifact  
deployment

Use the existing health/diagnostic infrastructure where available.  
Do not create the final system-wide Stage 16 Diagnostic Fabric here.  
This build only needs the local health information required to operate the Building System.  


RESOURCE GOVERNANCE

Integrate with the existing ResourceGovernor.  
Every major operation should be resource-aware:  

model invocation  
worker creation  
environment creation  
build  
process execution  
benchmark  
deployment

Before expensive work:  
resource availability→ estimate cost→ authorize→ execute→ record actual cost  
This allows Jarvis to choose cheaper mechanisms when they are sufficient.  


COMPUTE ADAPTATION

The system should eventually support adaptive execution:  
LOW COMPLEXITY→ deterministic mechanism  
MODERATE→ retrieval / small model  
HIGH→ reasoning model  
NOVEL / UNCERTAIN→ research + deep reasoning  
PARALLELIZABLE→ bounded workers  
This is where the LFM research principles become useful.  
Do not hardcode one model.  


WORKER ORCHESTRATION

Workers must be controlled by the central Development Orchestrator.  
The orchestrator owns:  

worker creation  
task assignment  
context allocation  
resource allocation  
cancellation  
result collection  
conflict handling  
worker termination

Workers do not create uncontrolled workers indefinitely.  


WORKER CONTRACT

Every worker must receive a bounded task contract:  

taskId  
objective  
inputs  
allowed capabilities  
workspace/environment  
resource budget  
deadline  
expected output

Every worker returns:  

status  
result  
evidence  
changes  
blockers  
confidence  
recommended next action

This keeps orchestration deterministic and inspectable.  


CONFLICT RESOLUTION

If workers produce conflicting results:  
Do not blindly merge them.  
The orchestrator should:  

identify conflict  
preserve both results  
compare evidence  
request additional analysis if necessary  
select or synthesize a result  
record the decision

Worker disagreement becomes evidence, not chaos.  


RESEARCH WORKER

The research worker should produce structured research output:  

question  
sources  
findings  
mechanisms  
limitations  
alternatives  
confidence  
recommendation

The worker should not directly modify Jarvis.  
Its result returns to the orchestrator.  


REPOSITORY WORKER

The repository worker should answer questions such as:  

where is X implemented?  
what depends on X?  
what files are relevant?  
what architecture is involved?  
what could this change affect?

It should prioritize Graphify/repository intelligence rather than repeatedly scanning everything.  


IMPLEMENTATION WORKER

The implementation worker may modify only its assigned environment/workspace.  
It returns:  

changes  
files affected  
build status  
blockers  
evidence

It cannot promote its own work.  


REVIEW WORKER

The review worker evaluates:  

requested behavior  
architecture  
compatibility  
unintended changes  
resource impact  
candidate quality

Its output becomes evidence for candidate evaluation.  


BENCHMARK WORKER

The benchmark worker runs the defined workload against candidates using identical measurement rules.  
It must not modify candidate implementation merely to improve its score.  


DEPLOYMENT WORKER

The deployment worker handles deployment mechanics.  
It does not decide whether a candidate deserves promotion.  
Promotion remains a separate policy decision.  


WORKER CANCELLATION

Any worker must be cancellable.  
Cancellation must:  

stop execution  
release resources  
preserve useful evidence  
update task state  
avoid leaving orphan processes



DEADLINE / BUDGET CONTROL

Every development session should have:  

time budget  
compute budget  
memory budget  
worker budget  
mutation budget  
repair iteration budget

The system must degrade gracefully when the budget is exhausted.  
It should report:  
"Insufficient budget to complete."  
rather than entering an endless loop.  


DEVELOPMENT STATE MACHINE

Create an explicit DevelopmentSession lifecycle:  
REQUESTED→ ANALYZING→ PLANNING→ RESEARCHING→ DESIGNING→ PREPARING→ BUILDING→ EXECUTING→ OBSERVING→ REPAIRING→ EVALUATING→ CANDIDATE_READY→ STAGING→ PROMOTING→ DEPLOYED→ COMPLETED  
Failure states:  
FAILEDBLOCKEDCANCELLEDABANDONEDROLLED_BACK  
State transitions must be explicit.  


RECOVERY

If the process itself is interrupted:  
Jarvis should be able to recover the DevelopmentSession from persistent state.  
It should determine:  

last known state  
active environment  
unfinished operation  
surviving processes  
retained evidence  
next safe action

Never assume that an interrupted process completed successfully.  


IDEMPOTENCY

Operations that may be retried should be idempotent where practical.  
Examples:  

environment initialization  
dependency installation  
artifact registration  
state transitions  
deployment preparation

Repeated execution must not corrupt the development state.  


CONCURRENCY CONTROL

Prevent multiple workers from silently modifying the same workspace state.  
Use explicit:  

ownership  
locks  
change sets  
branch/candidate isolation  
merge/reconciliation

Prefer separate candidate environments for competing implementations.  


CHANGE SETS

Represent groups of related modifications as a ChangeSet.  
A ChangeSet contains:  

changeSetId  
objective  
files  
operations  
environment  
parent version  
authoring worker  
evidence  
status

This gives Jarvis a clean unit for:  
reviewbenchmarkpromotionrollback  


MERGE / SYNTHESIS

When multiple candidates contain useful improvements, Jarvis may create a new candidate:  
Candidate A  



Candidate B→Candidate C  
But this must happen in a new mutated environment.  
Do not directly merge experimental candidates into LIVE.  


ALGORITHM LAB

Provide an abstraction for algorithm experiments.  
An AlgorithmExperiment should define:  

algorithm identity  
implementation  
input workload  
expected behavior  
metrics  
baseline  
candidate  
results

This should later become the foundation for Stage 7 Algorithm Discovery.  


BASELINE SYSTEM

Every benchmarkable candidate needs a baseline where appropriate.  
Compare:  
BASELINEvsCANDIDATE  
using the same workload and resource conditions.  
The baseline must be preserved so future improvements do not accidentally become regressions.  


REGRESSION PROTECTION

A candidate must be evaluated not only for the feature being changed but also for important known behavior.  
Record:  

baseline behavior  
candidate behavior  
regression signals

A faster implementation that silently destroys important behavior is not automatically an improvement.  


PROMOTION DECISION MODEL

Promotion should combine evidence rather than rely on one score.  
Consider:  

correctness  
required behavior  
benchmark improvement  
resource cost  
reliability  
compatibility  
regression risk  
confidence  
reversibility

The result should be:  
PROMOTEREJECTNEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE  
Do not force a binary decision when evidence is insufficient.  


PROMOTION RECORD

Every promotion must create a persistent record containing:  

candidate  
previous live version  
new live version  
evidence  
decision  
reason  
timestamp  
promotion policy  
rollback target

This is part of Jarvis's future self-understanding.  


DEPLOYMENT OBSERVATION

After deployment:  
deploy→ observe→ compare against expected behavior  
If health deteriorates:  
observe→ diagnose→ decide→ rollback or repair  
Do not automatically mutate LIVE without a defined policy.  


POST-DEPLOYMENT LEARNING

After a deployment reaches a stable outcome:  
experience→ evaluate→ extract lesson→ store in memory/knowledge graph  
The system should learn from both:  
successful deployments  
and:  
failed deployments / rollbacks.  


SELF-DEVELOPMENT LOOP

Once the generic system is working, Jarvis can target itself:  
Jarvis identifies improvement        ↓Research        ↓Design candidate        ↓Fork Jarvis        ↓Build candidate        ↓Run candidate        ↓Observe        ↓Benchmark        ↓Compare with current Jarvis        ↓Promote only if justified  
The important point is:  
Jarvis does not need to modify himself directly.  
He creates alternatives and evaluates them.  


SELF-EVOLUTION SAFETY

Self-evolution must remain bounded.  
Required controls:  

environment isolation  
resource limits  
change limits  
iteration limits  
promotion gates  
rollback  
lineage  
evidence  
human override where configured

Do not implement an uncontrolled recursive self-modification loop.  


PROJECT-INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE

The Building System must not contain Jarvis-specific assumptions in its core APIs.  
It should operate on:  
ProjectTargetWorkspaceEnvironmentCandidateExperimentArtifactDeploymentEvidenceDevelopmentSession  
Jarvis becomes one client of the Building System.  
This is what makes the system reusable.  


PLUGIN / ADAPTER ARCHITECTURE

External systems must enter through adapters.  
Examples:  
RepositoryAdapterBuildAdapterRuntimeAdapterEnvironmentAdapterDeploymentAdapterModelAdapterBenchmarkAdapterResearchAdapter  
Adapters must expose stable contracts.  
Do not spread vendor-specific logic throughout the cognitive layer.  


OFFLINE-FIRST

The Building System must remain useful offline.  
It should be capable of:  

repository analysis  
code modification  
local builds  
local execution  
local experiments  
local benchmarks  
local deployment  
local memory  
local model use

without requiring cloud services.  
Cloud resources may become optional accelerators later.  
Cloud Code is not a dependency of Jarvis.  


CLOUD CODE BOUNDARY

Cloud Code is an external development accelerator.  
It may be used NOW to build Jarvis.  
It must NOT become a runtime dependency of Jarvis.  
The finished Jarvis Building System must be capable of performing its own development lifecycle using Jarvis-native capabilities.  
Cloud Code may later become:  

an external research source  
an external worker  
an optional development capability

but never the foundation of Jarvis's existence.

HumanCore

The Building System becomes another major organ connected to the nervous system.

COGNITION     │     ↓BUILDING SYSTEM     │ ┌───┼─────────────┐ ↓   ↓             ↓RESEARCH  ENVIRONMENT  CAPABILITY     │        │         │     └────────┼─────────┘              ↓           EXECUTION              ↓          OBSERVATION              ↓           MEMORY              ↓           COGNITION

Do not bypass BodyCoordinator/event infrastructure.

Repair-B

- attempted solution
- environment
- change set
- result
- evidence

→ REPAIR
→ CHANGE
→ RESULT

This becomes reusable development knowledge.

- maximum repair iterations
- artifact retention
- evidence retention

→ benchmarking

→ mutated environments
→ comparison
→ promotion

Do not force maximum orchestration onto every task.

128. MINIMUM-COST PATH

For each objective, the Development Orchestrator should seek a sufficiently reliable path rather than automatically selecting the most powerful path.

Prefer:

existing capability
over

new implementation

Prefer:

deterministic mechanism
over

model reasoning

Prefer:

small model
over

large model

Prefer:

single worker
over

multiple workers

when they are sufficient.

Context must be assembled dynamically.

- environment identity
- evidence
- changes
- resource state

retry

destroy

or request intervention.

131. CRASH RECOVERY

If the Building System crashes:

On restart:

1. recover persistent sessions
2. inspect environments
3. inspect processes
4. inspect unfinished operations
5. reconcile known state
6. mark uncertain operations explicitly
7. choose safe recovery action

Never infer success merely because an operation record exists.

- processes
- workers
- environments
- temporary artifacts
- locks

RECORDED STATE
vs

environment still exists

record says BUILDING
process no longer exists

The system should detect and resolve these discrepancies safely.

141. SECURITY BOUNDARY

The Building System must treat environment execution as potentially dangerous.

credentials

resources

142. SECRET ISOLATION

credentials

143. NETWORK POLICY

Environment network access should be policy-controlled.

RESTRICTED

ALLOWED

144. EXPERIMENT CONTAMINATION CONTROL

An experiment must not silently depend on:

- undeclared host files
- undeclared environment variables

- pending operations
- important decisions
- known blockers
- evidence
- candidate state
- previous attempts
- lessons

This state must remain outside active model context.

The model receives a bounded projection.

============================================================
RESEARCH STAGE
============================================================

The building system must identify knowledge gaps.

Example:

Need capability X
→ Jarvis does not know how
→ research required

Then:

research
→ sources
→ extraction
→ mechanism
→ alternatives
→ limitations
→ synthesis

Do not turn this into a giant new web research subsystem.

Use the existing Universal Research direction as the conceptual interface.

The builder must request research rather than pretending it knows everything.

============================================================
MECHANISM EXTRACTION
============================================================

Research must not end with:

"Here is a library."

Instead:

Discovery
→ mechanism
→ abstraction
→ strengths
→ weaknesses
→ reusable principle
→ Jarvis-native design

This allows Jarvis to discover algorithms instead of merely importing software.

============================================================
ALGORITHM EXPERIMENTATION
============================================================

Jarvis must be able to create candidate algorithms.

Examples:

- retrieval algorithm
- ranking algorithm
- planning algorithm
- scheduler
- compression algorithm
- routing algorithm
- memory strategy
- orchestration policy

Treat algorithms as replaceable candidate mechanisms.

Algorithm A
Algorithm B
Algorithm C

→ same environment
→ same workload
→ same measurement
→ compare

This becomes the foundation for future Algorithm Discovery.

============================================================
CODE GENERATION
============================================================

Provide structured code-editing capabilities.

Support:

- create file
- read file
- modify file
- replace symbol
- add symbol
- remove symbol
- move code
- rename symbol
- patch
- generate component
- generate configuration

Every change must be associated with:

- operation
- environment
- workspace
- reason
- parent task

Do not permit uncontrolled modifications to live systems.

============================================================
COMMAND EXECUTION
============================================================

Create structured command execution.

Jarvis must execute:

- build commands
- package commands
- dependency managers
- scripts
- linters
- compilers
- smoke commands
- deployment commands

Execution must return structured:

- stdout
- stderr
- exit code
- duration
- process state
- resource information
- artifacts

Avoid returning giant unstructured logs by default.

============================================================
BUILD SYSTEM
============================================================

Detect and operate different project types.

At minimum support an abstraction capable of:

- Kotlin/Gradle
- Java
- Python
- JavaScript/TypeScript
- native/CMake
- shell-based projects

Use BuildAdapter.

Do not hardcode one project type.

More adapters must be possible later.

============================================================
DEPENDENCY MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Jarvis must be able to:

- detect missing dependencies
- propose dependencies
- install dependencies inside an environment
- pin versions
- record dependency changes
- rebuild
- detect dependency conflicts

Never mutate live merely to experiment with a dependency.

============================================================
BUILD / RUN / OBSERVE LOOP
============================================================

A builder task supports:

CHANGE
→ BUILD
→ RUN
→ OBSERVE
→ DIAGNOSE
→ REPAIR
→ BUILD AGAIN

The loop must be bounded.

Use:

- max iterations
- time budget
- resource budget
- change budget
- failure threshold

============================================================
FAILURE DIAGNOSIS
============================================================

Use existing failure/resilience architecture.

Do not create another failure system.

A build failure becomes structured evidence:

- command
- environment
- file
- location
- category
- error
- dependency
- likely cause
- attempted fix
- result

The next reasoning step consumes only relevant failure information.

============================================================
AUTOMATIC REPAIR LOOP
============================================================

Support:

failure
→ understand
→ locate cause
→ propose repair
→ apply repair in environment
→ rebuild

Repair remains environment-bound.

Live modification requires explicit promotion.

============================================================
BENCHMARKING
============================================================

Create universal benchmark abstraction.

Candidates may be measured by:

- correctness
- latency
- memory
- CPU
- output quality
- reliability
- resource cost
- success rate
- failure rate

Candidate comparisons must use the same workload.

Do not allow workload selection after seeing results.

============================================================
EXPERIMENT COMPARISON
============================================================

Support:

Candidate A
Candidate B
Candidate C

Each receives:

- environment
- version
- algorithm
- configuration
- benchmark
- evidence

Produce:

Candidate
Score
Cost
Performance
Failures
Confidence
Recommendation

Preserve raw evidence.

============================================================
PROMOTION GATE
============================================================

A candidate becomes live only through explicit promotion contract.

Promotion requires, where applicable:

- successful build
- required validation
- benchmark acceptance
- regression acceptance
- resource acceptance
- dependency validation
- environment integrity
- promotion policy approval

Never:

"it compiled"
→ automatically live.

============================================================
ROLLBACK
============================================================

Every promoted change must be reversible.

Maintain:

- previous version
- new version
- promotion evidence
- rollback point
- migration notes where necessary

Rollback is first-class.

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT FABRIC
============================================================

Create deployment abstraction:

artifact
→ package
→ stage
→ deploy
→ observe
→ confirm
→ promote

Future adapters may include:

- local process
- local service
- Android
- Docker
- VPS
- cloud
- other runtime environments

Do not implement every target now.

Implement common deployment contract.

============================================================
PROCESS / SERVICE MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Jarvis must eventually manage what he creates.

Support:

- start
- stop
- restart
- status
- health
- logs
- resource state
- crash detection

Experimental services must not become uncontrolled live dependencies.

============================================================
ARTIFACT MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Every build may produce:

- binaries
- APKs

- model artifacts
- configurations
- packages
- data

Artifacts contain:

- artifactId

- dependencies

- creation metadata

============================================================

============================================================

After deployment:

deployed system
→ health

→ failures
→ behavior

+

+

============================================================
LEARNING FROM BUILDS
============================================================

Every development attempt should generate reusable experience.

Record:

- task

- failures
- repairs
- successful approach
- unsuccessful approaches

- final outcome
- confidence

Use existing memory architecture.

Do not create another memory store.

============================================================
LESSON EXTRACTION
============================================================

After development:

experience
→ extract lesson
→ determine reuse potential
→ store

Examples:

"Build system required X."

"This failure pattern usually means Y."

"Algorithm A beats B under memory pressure."

"Library X causes conflict with Y."

These lessons later improve the builder.

============================================================
PRIME-AGENT MECHANISMS
============================================================

From Prime-Agent research, extract mechanisms around:

- externalized persistent state
- small active context
- bounded workers
- delegation
- lineage
- iterative repair
- learning from outcomes

Do not replicate Prime-Agent's exact implementation.

Jarvis remains owner of cognition.

============================================================
MEM0 MECHANISMS
============================================================

Extract and adapt:

- memory extraction
- memory consolidation
- selective retrieval
- history preservation
- relationship-aware retrieval
- evidence-backed memory

Use existing Jarvis memory architecture.

Do not create Mem0 inside Jarvis.

============================================================
MULTI-AGENT MECHANISMS
============================================================

Use multi-agent concepts only where they improve actual development throughput.

Possible bounded roles:

- Research Worker
- Repository Worker
- Implementation Worker
- Review Worker
- Benchmark Worker
- Deployment Worker

These are workers, not independent Jarvis personalities.

Central Jarvis remains orchestrator.

Every worker:

- receives one bounded task
- receives only relevant context
- operates inside bounded environment
- returns structured result
- exits

No permanent uncontrolled swarm.

============================================================
PARALLELIZATION
============================================================

When PlanGraph determines tasks are independent:

A ─────→ result
B ─────→ result
C ─────→ result

execute concurrently.

When dependencies exist:

A → B → C

remain sequential.

Reuse existing planning/dependency architecture.

============================================================
LFM MECHANISMS
============================================================

LFM is a research seed for:

- efficient local inference
- small-model specialization
- adaptive compute
- low-memory execution
- retrieval specialization
- model specialization
- edge deployment
- compute-per-task optimization

Use these principles in the builder.

The system should eventually select:

tiny model
small model
standard model
deep model
specialized model
deterministic mechanism

depending on task.

Do not hardcode one vendor.

============================================================
DEVELOPMENT INTELLIGENCE ROUTING
============================================================

For every development task ask:

Can deterministic tooling solve this?

Can retrieval solve this?

Can a small model solve this?

Can one worker solve this?

Does this require deep reasoning?

Does this require research?

Does this require multiple workers?

Spend expensive computation only when necessary.

============================================================
MODEL MEMORY MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Protect system RAM.

Eventually support:

load small model
→ perform cheap work
→ unload
→ load deep model
→ perform difficult work
→ unload
→ restore lightweight model

Do not require all models resident simultaneously.

============================================================
WORKER MEMORY MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Workers must not receive:

- complete repository
- complete memory
- complete world model
- complete task history

Each receives only required context.

This is a major context/RAM optimization.

============================================================
DEVELOPMENT SESSION
============================================================

Create DevelopmentSession concept.

It represents one complete development objective.

Contains:

- session ID
- objective
- workspace
- environment
- plan
- workers
- changes
- build results
- failures
- repairs
- benchmarks
- candidate
- promotion state
- lessons

Session should survive interruption where practical.

============================================================
DEVELOPMENT LINEAGE
============================================================

Jarvis must know:

Why was this code changed?

Which task caused it?

Which research finding caused it?

Which algorithm was selected?

Which candidate environment produced it?

Which benchmark approved it?

Which promotion created the live version?

This is essential for future self-evolution.

============================================================
SELF-DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION
============================================================

System must target:

- normal software projects
- eventually Jarvis itself

Do not hardcode Jarvis repository as only project.

Use:

ProjectTarget

which can point to:

- Jarvis
- another repository
- another workspace
- another project

Same development system operates on all.

============================================================
JARVIS SELF-EVOLUTION BOUNDARY
============================================================

When target is Jarvis itself:

LIVE JARVIS
    ↓
SNAPSHOT
    ↓
MUTATED JARVIS ENVIRONMENT
    ↓
CHANGE
    ↓
BUILD
    ↓
RUN
    ↓
BENCHMARK
    ↓
COMPARE TO CURRENT
    ↓
PROMOTION DECISION

Never:

Jarvis rewrites live Jarvis directly.

This boundary is permanent.

============================================================
CAPABILITY FABRIC INTEGRATION
============================================================

All development operations should eventually be capabilities.

Examples:

- READ_FILE
- WRITE_FILE
- PATCH_FILE
- SEARCH_CODE
- QUERY_GRAPH
- RUN_COMMAND

- START_PROCESS
- STOP_PROCESS
- CREATE_ENVIRONMENT
- DESTROY_ENVIRONMENT
- RUN_BENCHMARK
- DEPLOY
- ROLLBACK
- INSPECT_FAILURE

Use existing Capability Fabric.

Do not create a new tool registry.

============================================================
EXECUTION INTEGRATION
============================================================

Development operations must flow through existing execution architecture where applicable:

PlanGraph
→ ActionRequest
→ Capability
→ CapabilityInvoker
→ result

Do not bypass:

- immune layer
- permissions
- capability lifecycle
- resource policy
- failure surface

Building System is an extension of existing execution organism, not a parallel execution architecture.

============================================================
PERMISSIONS
============================================================

Development operations have explicit permission categories.

Examples:

- READ_WORKSPACE
- WRITE_WORKSPACE
- EXECUTE_PROCESS
- INSTALL_DEPENDENCY
- CREATE_ENVIRONMENT
- DEPLOY
- PROMOTE
- ROLLBACK

Distinguish:

EXPERIMENTAL PERMISSION

from:

LIVE-SYSTEM PERMISSION

Experimental permissions may be broader.

Live promotion permissions are stricter.

============================================================
LIVE SYSTEM PROTECTION
============================================================

Builder knows difference between:

EXPERIMENTAL
STAGED
LIVE

EXPERIMENTAL:

Anything permitted within configured environment limits.

STAGED:

Deployment candidate; isolated.

LIVE:

Controlled and protected.

No experimental mutation silently crosses boundary.

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT ESCALATION
============================================================

Explicit progression:

EXPERIMENT
→ CANDIDATE
→ STAGED
→ LIVE

Promotion is deliberate.

Rollback:

LIVE
→ PREVIOUS LIVE

without deleting evidence.

============================================================
BUILDER API
============================================================

Expose high-level operation conceptually similar to:

buildProject(request)

Request may specify:

- target
- objective
- constraints
- environment policy
- resource budget
- deadline
- deployment policy
- success criteria

Return BuildResult containing:

- success
- candidate
- environment
- artifacts
- benchmark
- failures
- changes
- promotion recommendation
- evidence
- lessons

Adapt names to repository conventions.

Do not force exact class names if equivalent domain abstractions exist.

============================================================
EXPERIMENT API
============================================================

Provide conceptual:

runExperiment(specification)

Lifecycle:

create environment
→ apply candidate
→ execute
→ observe
→ benchmark
→ preserve evidence
→ destroy or retain

Experiment has lifecycle and persistent identity.

============================================================
DEPLOY API
============================================================

Provide conceptual:

deploy(candidate)

with explicit policy gates.

Deployment cannot bypass promotion policy.

Deployment remains separate from promotion.

============================================================
ROLLBACK API
============================================================

Provide conceptual:

rollback(deploymentId)

Preserve:

- reason
- source deployment
- target version
- evidence
- resulting state

Rollback creates auditable operation record.

============================================================
ENVIRONMENT DESTRUCTION
============================================================

When environment destroyed:

Delete runtime state.

Preserve:

- experiment metadata
- source snapshot
- benchmark results
- failure evidence
- lessons
- candidate lineage
- relevant artifacts

The reality disappears.

Its knowledge does not.

============================================================
REPRODUCIBILITY
============================================================

Every experiment reproducible as far as practical.

Record:

- source version
- environment specification
- dependency versions
- configuration
- model used
- worker configuration
- algorithm candidate
- benchmark workload
- resource policy

Jarvis can recreate experiment from specification rather than hidden state.

============================================================

============================================================

References:

- status
- promotion eligibility

States:

PROPOSED
→ BUILDING
→ RUNNING
→ EVALUATED
→ PROMOTABLE
→ PROMOTED

or:

REJECTED
FAILED
ABANDONED

============================================================
CANDIDATE LINEAGE
============================================================

Candidates form genealogy.

Example:

CURRENT
 ├── Candidate-A
 │    ├── Candidate-A1
 │    └── Candidate-A2
 │
 └── Candidate-B
      └── Candidate-B1

Jarvis determines:

- parent
- descendants
- modifications
- benchmark differences
- why branch selected/rejected

Essential for algorithm discovery and self-evolution.

============================================================
EXPERIMENT SPECIFICATION

Create declarative ExperimentSpecification.

Defines:

- base state

- environment requirements

- workload

- benchmark criteria
- timeout
- iteration limits
- retention policy

Serializable.

Experiment describable independently of active model context.

============================================================

Major operations:

- environment creation

- file modification
- command execution
- build
- repair
- benchmark
- deployment
- promotion
- rollback
- destruction

Do not retain enormous raw logs indefinitely.

Store structured metadata plus references to retained evidence.

============================================================

============================================================

Create common Evidence abstraction.

- benchmark result
- resource measurement
- deployment health
- model output
- research finding
- comparison result

Important development decisions must be traceable to evidence.

============================================================
OBSERVATION MODEL
============================================================

Create structured observations rather than passing raw logs directly into cognition.

Observation may contain:

- timestamp

- evidence reference

Observation usable by:

- diagnosis

- future improvement

============================================================
HEALTH MODEL
============================================================

Building System exposes health for:

- environment
- workspace

- artifact
- deployment

Use existing health/diagnostic infrastructure.

Do not create final system-wide Stage 16 Diagnostic Fabric.

============================================================
RESOURCE GOVERNANCE
============================================================

Integrate existing ResourceGovernor.

Every major operation resource-aware:

- model invocation

- environment creation
- build
- process execution
- benchmark
- deployment

resource availability
→ estimate cost
→ authorize
→ execute
→ record actual cost

Allows Jarvis to choose cheaper mechanisms when sufficient.

============================================================
COMPUTE ADAPTATION
============================================================

Eventually support:

LOW COMPLEXITY

MODERATE

HIGH

NOVEL / UNCERTAIN

PARALLELIZABLE

Use LFM research principles.

Do not hardcode one model.

============================================================
WORKER ORCHESTRATION
============================================================

Workers controlled by central Development Orchestrator.

Orchestrator owns:

- worker creation
- task assignment
- context allocation
- resource allocation
- cancellation
- result collection
- conflict handling
- worker termination

Workers cannot create uncontrolled workers indefinitely.

============================================================
WORKER CONTRACT
============================================================

Every worker receives:

- taskId
- objective
- inputs
- allowed capabilities
- workspace/environment
- resource budget
- deadline
- expected output

Returns:

- status
- result
- evidence
- changes
- blockers
- confidence
- recommended next action

Keeps orchestration deterministic and inspectable.

============================================================
CONFLICT RESOLUTION
============================================================

If workers conflict:

1. identify conflict
2. preserve both results
3. compare evidence
4. request additional analysis if necessary
5. select or synthesize result
6. record decision

Worker disagreement becomes evidence, not chaos.

============================================================
RESEARCH WORKER
============================================================

Produces structured research:

- question
- sources
- findings
- mechanisms
- limitations
- alternatives
- confidence
- recommendation

Must not directly modify Jarvis.

Result returns to orchestrator.

============================================================
REPOSITORY WORKER
============================================================

Answers:

- where is X implemented?
- what depends on X?
- what files are relevant?
- what architecture is involved?
- what could this change affect?

Prioritize Graphify/repository intelligence over repeated whole-repository scanning.

============================================================
IMPLEMENTATION WORKER
============================================================

May modify only assigned environment/workspace.

Returns:

- changes
- files affected
- build status
- blockers
- evidence

Cannot promote its own work.

============================================================
REVIEW WORKER
============================================================

Evaluates:

- requested behavior
- architecture
- compatibility
- unintended changes
- resource impact
- candidate quality

Output becomes candidate evidence.

============================================================
BENCHMARK WORKER
============================================================

Runs defined workload against candidates using identical measurement rules.

Must not modify candidate implementation merely to improve score.

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT WORKER
============================================================

Handles deployment mechanics.

Does not decide whether candidate deserves promotion.

Promotion remains separate policy decision.

============================================================
WORKER CANCELLATION
============================================================

Any worker must be cancellable.

Cancellation:

- stops execution
- releases resources
- preserves useful evidence
- updates task state
- avoids orphan processes

============================================================
DEADLINE / BUDGET CONTROL
============================================================

Every development session has:

- time budget
- compute budget
- memory budget
- worker budget
- mutation budget
- repair iteration budget

Gracefully degrade when budget exhausted.

Report:

"Insufficient budget to complete."

Never enter endless loop.

============================================================
DEVELOPMENT STATE MACHINE
============================================================

DevelopmentSession lifecycle:

REQUESTED
→ ANALYZING
→ PLANNING
→ RESEARCHING
→ DESIGNING
→ PREPARING
→ BUILDING
→ EXECUTING
→ OBSERVING
→ REPAIRING
→ EVALUATING
→ CANDIDATE_READY
→ STAGING
→ PROMOTING
→ DEPLOYED
→ COMPLETED

Failure states:

FAILED
BLOCKED
CANCELLED

ROLLED_BACK

State transitions explicit.

============================================================
RECOVERY
============================================================

If development process interrupted:

Recover DevelopmentSession from persistent state.

Determine:

- last known state
- active environment
- unfinished operation
- surviving processes
- retained evidence
- next safe action

Never assume interrupted process completed successfully.

============================================================
IDEMPOTENCY
============================================================

Operations retried should be idempotent where practical.

Examples:

- environment initialization
- dependency installation
- artifact registration
- state transitions
- deployment preparation

Repeated execution must not corrupt development state.

============================================================
CONCURRENCY CONTROL
============================================================

Prevent workers from silently modifying same workspace.

Use explicit:

- ownership
- locks
- change sets
- branch/candidate isolation
- merge/reconciliation

Prefer separate candidate environments for competing implementations.

============================================================

============================================================

Contains:

- changeSetId

- parent version
- authoring worker
- evidence
- status

Clean unit for:

- review
- benchmark
- promotion
- rollback

============================================================
MERGE / SYNTHESIS
============================================================

Candidate A
+
Candidate B
→
Candidate C

This occurs in a new mutated environment.

Never directly merge experimental candidates into LIVE.

============================================================
ALGORITHM LAB
============================================================

Provide abstraction for algorithm experiments.

- algorithm identity
- implementation
- input workload
- expected behavior
- metrics
- baseline
- candidate

Foundation for Stage 7 Algorithm Discovery.

============================================================
BASELINE SYSTEM
============================================================

Every benchmarkable candidate needs baseline where appropriate.

Compare:

BASELINE
vs
CANDIDATE

same workload
same resource conditions.

Baseline preserved so improvements do not become regressions.

============================================================
REGRESSION PROTECTION
============================================================

Evaluate not only requested feature but important known behavior.

Record:

- baseline behavior
- candidate behavior
- regression signals

Faster implementation that destroys important behavior is not automatically improvement.

============================================================
PROMOTION DECISION MODEL
============================================================

Promotion combines evidence.

Consider:

- correctness
- required behavior
- benchmark improvement
- resource cost
- reliability
- compatibility
- regression risk
- confidence
- reversibility

Output:

PROMOTE
REJECT
NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE

Do not force binary decision when evidence insufficient.

============================================================

============================================================

- candidate
- previous live version
- new live version
- evidence
- decision
- reason
- timestamp
- promotion policy
- rollback target

This contributes to future self-understanding.

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT OBSERVATION
============================================================

After deployment:

observe
→ diagnose
→ decide
→ rollback or repair

============================================================
POST-DEPLOYMENT LEARNING
============================================================

After stable deployment:

experience
→ evaluate

Learn from:

- successful deployments
- failed deployments
- rollbacks

============================================================
SELF-DEVELOPMENT LOOP
============================================================

        ↓

        ↓
